Completed all requirements of the doctoral degree no more than three years before September 1 of the year of application (extensions up to three years for career interruptions, relevant industry/government employment, caregiving)
Not hold or be on leave from a tenure-track or tenured faculty position
Apply to only one Canada Research Training Awards Suite program per academic year; maximum three lifetime applications to the CPRA
Have not already received a postdoctoral award from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC (including a Banting Postdoctoral Fellowship); cannot hold a CPRA concurrently with another tri-agency research training award

International applicants must be registered in, have completed a doctoral degree at, or be currently conducting postdoctoral research at a Canadian institution; up to 20% of awards are available to international applicants
Up to 30% of awards may be held outside Canada, restricted to Canadian citizens, permanent residents or protected persons who completed their doctorate at a Canadian institution
CPRAs cannot be held at a Canadian federal government research institution

Research appraisal form completed by the proposed supervisor at the primary place of tenure
Institutional Nomination and Commitment form completed by the department head or designate at the proposed institution
Mandatory diversity considerations in research design module (not subject to merit review)

Quality of proposed research program (50%): originality and potential significance, feasibility, appropriateness of the intended place of tenure, effectiveness of institutional support
A score of 3.0 or higher on each criterion is required to be recommended for funding

official.description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award program recognizes and empowers the next generation of highly qualified innovators, knowledge workers and creative thinkers. It supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers in developing their research skills and provides the funding and flexibility needed to support their contributions to building world-class research capacity and to Canada's prosperity and competitiveness.

official.english_requirement: Applications may be submitted in either of Canada's official languages, English or French; all required components including PDF attachments must be in English and/or French, and supporting documents in other languages require a certified translation

applicant_utility.summary: This is a $70,000-per-year, two-year stipend for postdoctoral researchers who completed their doctorate within the last three years, offered through an annual autumn competition (SSHRC deadline September 10). The application is only as strong as its two referee appraisals, the supervisor's research appraisal and the institutional nomination, because none of those components are in your control on deadline day. Because SSHRC and CIHR applicants may face host-institution endorsement deadlines well before the agency deadline, confirm your institution's internal date first and build the package around it. Budget realistically: the award is taxable income in Canada and the published pages do not promise tuition or relocation coverage, so plan to cover those yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent PhD graduates within three years of degree completion who can secure a strong supervisor and institutional nomination at a Canadian (or, for citizens/PRs, foreign) research institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your host institution's internal nomination deadline, which can fall well before the agency deadline
Ask two referees early - one normally your doctoral supervisor - and check their invitation emails have not been caught by spam filters
Brief your proposed supervisor so the Research Appraisal form arrives before the deadline, and identify the department head or designate for the Institutional Nomination and Commitment form
Draft the four-page program of work in plain language for a multidisciplinary committee, explicitly showing how it goes beyond your thesis
Verify every page of the online form and confirm both referee forms are completed, since unverified sections block submission
Check PDF attachments against the specified margins, font size, page length and file size rules before uploading
common_rejection_risks: Two referee appraisals, the supervisor research appraisal or the institutional nomination arriving after the deadline - the system rejects incomplete applications
Research too close to the doctoral thesis, which fails the 'significantly distinct' rule
Choosing the wrong merit review committee or the wrong agency, sending the file to reviewers outside the discipline
A tenure-track or tenured appointment, a prior tri-agency postdoctoral award, or more than three lifetime applications, which end eligibility outright
Last-minute uploads that fail the margin, font or page-length specifications and are deemed ineligible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published pages do not state tuition, travel or relocation coverage, so applicants should assume they must fund tuition (where charged by the host), moving costs and any research expenses themselves; the stipend is also taxed as Canadian income with no deductions at source.
document_audit: Program of work is capped at four pages and must not use footnotes or refer reviewers to URLs - exceptions apply only to research-creation samples
Bibliography (10 pages) and research contributions (two pages) are separate files with their own caps, and co-author roles must be stated for each item
Applicants who hold any teaching appointment must attach the teaching appointment letter or a letter confirming they do not hold a tenured/tenure-track position
The diversity considerations module is mandatory but is not shared with the committee and is not merit reviewed
alerts: SSHRC's Submit button disappears at 8:00 p.m. sharp on deadline day, and the system is heavily loaded in the final hours - submit days early
After the deadline you cannot change the application except personal contact information, and submissions are deleted 30 days after the deadline
The award can start on the first of any month between April 2027 and January 2028, and all degree requirements must be finished by December 31, 2027 at the latest
Only 20% of awards go to international applicants, and roughly 30% may be held outside Canada and only by citizens, permanent residents or protected persons
Priority research areas (AI, defence, health, clean technology and similar) attract additional award offers, so name them in your keywords if your work genuinely aligns
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Applicant completes and verifies the online form and web CV, referees and supervisor submit their forms through the same system, the institution submits the nomination, then SSHRC staff checks completeness and forwards eligible files to the multidisciplinary merit review committee.

official.deadline_note: This is the institutional deadline: Canadian institutions must submit online applications on behalf of candidates and email the ranking of applications by 11:59 p.m. EDT, March 24, 2026. Institutions are encouraged to establish an earlier deadline with candidates and their home institutions.
official.status_note: The official page states 'Application period for 2026-27 is closed.' The next cycle's application dates were not published as at 2026-10-10.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Tuition must be waived by Canadian institutions' - tuition is waived by the host institution rather than paid out of the scholarship.
benefits: Airfare via the most direct and economical route
Living expenses, such as accommodation, utilities and food

Books and supplies required for the study or research, excluding computers and other equipment
eligibility: Citizen of an ASEAN Member State (including Timor-Leste), a listed Pacific Island Country (Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu) or Mongolia
Enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country
Paying tuition fees to that institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the exchange

Not eligible if holding or applying for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, already participating in another Government of Canada-funded scholarship, already enrolled in a Canadian degree/diploma/certificate program, or a previous SEED (phase 1) recipient
Canadian host institutions must be Designated Learning Institutions, must waive tuition fees for recipients, and must centralize all applications through their international office
requirements: Canadian host institution must apply on behalf of the candidate through My EduCanada
One-page letter of intent that identifies the Sustainable Development Goal the proposed study or research aligns with - letters without an SDG are deemed incomplete and not eligible
Country-specific explanation of how learning in Canada will help reduce poverty in the home country (or, for Brunei, Singapore and Cook Islands candidates, in another eligible country)
One-page letter of invitation from the Canadian supervisor for graduate applicants
Supporting documents each smaller than 5 MB, in .jpg, .gif, .png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt or .xlsx format
Documents in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by a translation; revised documents are not accepted after the deadline
documents: Proof of citizenship: copy of passport or national identity card with photo and valid dates (driver's licence, permanent residence card, work permit, student card, health card, birth certificate or baptismal certificate are not accepted)
Signed Privacy Notice Statement for non-Canadian participants, dated within the last six months
Letter of intent from the candidate (maximum one page)
Letter of proof of full-time enrolment from the home institution, on official letterhead and dated within the last six months (transcripts, student cards and admission letters are not acceptable)
Letter of support from the home institution (maximum one page), on official letterhead and dated within the last six months
Letter of invitation from the Canadian supervisor (graduate applicants only, maximum one page)
Institutional ranking of applications emailed to the scholarship administrator (seed-bpeed@international.gc.ca) with each candidate's MyEduCanada application number
selection_criteria: Linkage of the proposed research or study in Canada to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development
The candidate's commitment to use their proposed research or studies in Canada to help reduce poverty and narrow the development gap in their country or region
Merit of the research or study to be undertaken in Canada
Benefit to the home institution and peers; benefit to the Canadian institution, supervisor and peers
Rankings submitted by the Canadian institution
coverage: Eligible expenses: visa or study/work permit fees; airfare via the most direct and economical route; health insurance; living expenses such as accommodation, utilities and food; ground transportation including a public transportation pass; books and supplies required for the study or research, excluding computers and other equipment
Tuition must be waived by Canadian institutions
application_method: The Canadian institution assigns a program coordinator and creates an account through Global Affairs Canada Single Sign-On (a GCKey account is recommended), registering with account type Institution
The coordinator selects the SEED-2 program on My EduCanada, clicks Apply, enters the candidate data and clicks Validate and save throughout the form
The institution uploads all required supporting documents (each under 5 MB in an accepted format)
The institution reads and accepts the Declaration and permission statement and clicks Submit, receiving a confirmation message and reference number
The institution separately emails its ranking of applications to seed-bpeed@international.gc.ca, indicating each candidate's MyEduCanada application number
official.application_route: Students cannot apply directly: a Canadian host institution applies on their behalf through My EduCanada, so the first step is contacting the international office of a Canadian DLI with an exchange link to the home institution
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of ASEAN Member States, listed Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia; candidates must not hold or have a pending application for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, and must return to their home institution after the exchange
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme exists specifically for students from eligible Indo-Pacific countries; eligibility is by citizenship of the listed countries, not by residence in Canada
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Study or research must contribute to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and the letter of intent must identify a specific SDG
official.research_requirement: Graduate applicants must obtain a one-page invitation letter from the Canadian supervisor describing the research collaboration; selected candidates must abstain from clinical training or clinically-oriented research involving direct patient care
official.duration: Four months to eight months: college/undergraduate 4 months or 8 months (two academic terms); graduate 4 months or 5-6 months. Scholarships cannot be deferred and are not renewable.
official.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy that expands the Canada-ASEAN SEED programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia. It provides opportunities to conduct short-term study or research at Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas that contribute to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, aiming to reduce poverty in eligible countries and strengthen people-to-people ties with the Indo-Pacific region.
official.program_type: Government short-term exchange scholarship (Indo-Pacific Strategy initiative)
official.english_requirement: Not stated as an applicant requirement; the official page states that documents in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by a translation

verification.notes: All four award values ($10,200, $12,700, $15,900), the March 24, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EDT) institutional deadline and the eligible-expenses list were confirmed on the official SEED-2 page on the educanada.ca domain; funding_amount records the base four-month value because the value varies by component, and the page confirms the 2026-27 application period is closed.

applicant_utility.summary: SEED-2 funds a four-to-eight-month exchange in Canada for students from ASEAN states, Pacific Island countries and Mongolia, with values from $10,200 to $15,900 plus tuition waived by the Canadian host. You cannot apply yourself: a Canadian institution submits the application on your behalf through My EduCanada by March 24, 2026 (for the closed 2026-27 round), so your real task is securing a Canadian host partnership months earlier. Build the package around the one-page letter of intent, because a letter that does not name a specific Sustainable Development Goal is rejected outright, and every supporting letter must be on official letterhead and dated within the last six months. Plan to arrive in Canada between August 1, 2026 and February 1, 2027, since the exchange is non-deferrable and you must return to your home institution afterwards.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Full-time undergraduate or graduate students in the 30 eligible Indo-Pacific countries whose home institution has an exchange link with a Canadian Designated Learning Institution willing to waive tuition and nominate them.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify a Canadian host institution that is a Designated Learning Institution and is willing to waive tuition and centralize the application through its international office
For graduate applicants, secure a Canadian supervisor and a one-page invitation letter describing the research collaboration

Write the one-page letter of intent that names a specific SDG and, for eligible countries, explains how the exchange will reduce poverty in the home country (or, for Brunei, Singapore and Cook Islands, in another eligible country)
Request the enrolment proof and support letters from your home institution early, on official letterhead and dated within six months of submission
Prepare a passport copy or national ID as proof of citizenship - driver's licences, student cards and birth certificates are refused
Give the institution your documents well before its internal cut-off, since no revised documents are accepted after the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Letter of intent that omits an SDG - deemed incomplete and not eligible regardless of merit
Full-time enrolment letter that fails to confirm full-time status, or that is a transcript, student card or admission letter instead of a letter
Letters dated more than six months before submission, or missing official letterhead
Losing the tuition waiver, which the Canadian institution must guarantee for college and undergraduate study
Being in a Government of Canada-funded scholarship already, enrolled in a Canadian program, or a previous SEED phase-one recipient
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scholarship covers airfare, insurance, local transport, living costs, books and permit fees, with tuition waived by the host, but computers and other equipment are excluded and any costs beyond the fixed component value are the student's responsibility.
document_audit: Every file must be under 5 MB and in .jpg, .gif, .png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt or .xlsx - oversized or other formats will not upload
The Privacy Notice Statement for non-Canadian participants must be signed and dated within the last six months
Non-English or non-French documents need a translation attached, and nothing can be revised after the deadline
The institutional ranking email with each candidate's MyEduCanada number is part of a complete submission, so confirm the coordinator has sent it
alerts: The route runs entirely through Canadian institutions - students who contact Global Affairs Canada directly will be redirected to their host or home institution
The award is non-deferrable and non-renewable, and failure to arrive in Canada within the arrival window can cancel the scholarship
Selected candidates must abstain from clinical training or clinically-oriented research involving direct patient care
Scholarships are subject to availability of Government of Canada funding, so a published cycle is not a guarantee of offers
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Candidate assembles documents with the home and Canadian institutions, the Canadian institution's coordinator enters and validates the application in My EduCanada, uploads all files, accepts the declaration and submits, then separately emails the ranking to the administrator before the deadline.
